crisis.label: High
crisis.detail: Sep 3: Al Jazeera reported the heaviest US-Iran exchange in over a month - CENTCOM struck Iranian sites (Sirik, Konarak, Bandar Abbas, Jask, Asaluyeh, Ahvaz, Qeshm) on Sep 1, killing roughly 12; Iran retaliated early Sep 2 with a multi-front barrage on US-linked bases in Jordan (13 missiles, 10 intercepted), Bahrain (drones on Sheikh Isa airbase), Kuwait (intercepted drones/missiles) and Iraq's Erbil (IRGC claims a destroyed repair centre). No US casualties reported. Brent eased to $95.45 (-0.19%) and WTI to $90.97 (-0.05%) on Sep 3 (Trading Economics) as the prior spike partially consolidates; JKM CFD is $23.76 (+0.61%, Trading Economics, Sep 2); TTF confirmed at 73.36 EUR/MWh (Yahoo Finance, Sep 2). QatarEnergy force majeure remains extended into early November. Crisis level remains 4 (High) given interceptions held and no new Hormuz closure event; probabilities shift toward tail on the widened four-country exchange: base 5%, stress 50%, tail 45%.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and Oman advance a temporary corridor and mine-clearance framework; a signed, monitored reopening restores traffic and lowers Brent toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained into early November.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The corridor remains provisional and traffic stays selective under Iranian fees, sanctions pressure and residual mine and attack risk; Brent holds $85-105 and JKM stays elevated while Qatar's force majeure runs into early November.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: A widened multi-front exchange, a failed framework or renewed tanker attacks could close the southern lane again and spill into Bab el-Mandeb; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.
